title: Plant Manager
summary: Keep plant records and care tasks together, with a map/placement extension and Home Assistant reminders. The underlying plant-record application is HortusFox; this repository contains the custom integration and deployment work around it, not a claim of authorship over HortusFox.
features: Organise names, photos, locations and notes in the underlying plant application.
Track watering, fertilising and other tasks with their own dates/recurrence.
The custom worker schedules the next occurrence after processing completion.
Send due/overdue summaries through a configured HA mobile notification target.
Use the hosted plant-map extension alongside care records.
Optional connected Pl@ntNet recognition sends the selected photo to that service.
workflows: Choose Add Plant and enter a useful name and location. Add a clear photo and notes that help distinguish it from similar plants.
Keep identification uncertainty explicit. A probable identification should not silently become a confirmed species.
Use Search or Locations to return to the plant; the map is a placement aid rather than a replacement for its care record.
Open Tasks and Create new. Give the task a clear action, description and due date. Associate it with the relevant plant through the task/plant controls.
Keep watering and fertiliser schedules separate. Set recurrence only when appropriate for that task.
After checking the plant and performing the care, mark the task done. The custom recurrence worker advances from processing completion; overdue work stays due until completed.
Review the due/overdue list before acting. A notification is a prompt to inspect conditions, not an instruction to water dry and wet pots alike.
Open the plant history or completed-task list to check what was actually recorded.
If recurrence/reminders stop, inspect the custom worker and HA connection. Do not also enable an independent recurrence cron that advances tasks regardless of completion.
Use the identification/quick-scan control and choose a clear photo only if you intend to send it to the configured recognition service.
Compare the candidates with visible plant characteristics; keep uncertainty in the record.
Recognition credentials belong in the protected application configuration, not in an exported project or public issue.
limits: HortusFox and its dependencies retain their upstream licences. This package requires the underlying plant application, database, gateway and configured reminder worker. The demo simulates a care queue without sending notifications.
